title: Telemetry hardening playbook — collector interop & terraform notes
content:
Purpose and scope

This note is a practical playbook for hardening observability in private deployments (VPC/on-prem). It focuses on:
- upgrading and running OTEL Collectors with mixed exporter topologies,
- Prometheus/Grafana operational practices in isolated networks, and
- Terraform module patterns to make upgrades repeatable and low-risk.

Audience
- infra engineers doing private deployment rollouts
- SREs responsible for metrics/logs during upgrades
- Solutions engineering who will advise customers on safe upgrade windows

High-level goals
1) Make collector upgrades safe via canary and dual-export patterns.
2) Reduce data loss risk when migrating remote_write or log sinks.
3) Keep Prometheus and Grafana provisioning codified and reproducible.
4) Provide clear rollback and verification steps that are runnable without external internet access.

Quick summary of approach
- Use side-by-side collector instances (vX + vX+1) with routing rules to replicate data streams for a week before cutover.
- Configure Prometheus remote_write to a shim exporter for short-term buffering during migrations.
- Provision Grafana dashboards as YAML in Terraform so dashboards are consistent and can be rolled back.
- Pin module versions and expose small, well-documented flags for behavioral changes (e.g., batching, compression).

Collector upgrade pattern (safe canary + dual-write)
Prereq: access to private cluster, ephemeral jumpbox with credentials, CI pipeline that can apply Terraform in that VPC.
Steps:
1) Build new collector config and container image (tagged by date and semver, e.g. otel-collector:0.76.0-20241201).
2) Deploy as a new Deployment/DaemonSet alongside the existing collector (label new: telemetry-version=v2).
3) Configure new collector to mirror inputs from the same pipelines and to export to a second (test) backend: e.g., remote_write -> test-prometheus-receiver AND primary remote_write. For logs, set exporter to both primary ELK/S3 bucket and a test S3 prefix.
4) Verify metrics parity: compare counts for key series over 1–3 hours. Use query: sum(rate(my_service_requests_total[5m])) grouped by job. Expect <0.5% divergence after warm-up.
5) Run a traffic acceptance window (48–72 hours). If anomalies appear, adjust config and iterate; there is no user-facing impact because primary path still accepts traffic.
6) When stable, flip data consumers (if necessary) to point to the new collector endpoint and remove the legacy collector after another stability window.

Operational checks during rollout
- CPU/memory profiles of new pod vs old pod (kubectl top pods). New collector must be within 1.5x of baseline or have documented config changes.
- Exporter queue lengths and retry rates (otel_collector_exporter_retry_count metric).
- Prometheus scrape durations and missed scrapes. Use prometheus_target_interval_length_seconds summary.
- Log shipping lag: for S3-based sinks measure time between event timestamp and object creation.

Prometheus & remote_write migration notes
Patterns we use: local TSDB for short-term retention + remote_write for long-term. When changing remote targets:
- Add new remote_write block instead of replacing: remote_write: [primary, next].
- Use a short-term buffer (thanos receive / gateway) when moving between cloud-backed long-term stores.
- Terraform: expose remote_write endpoints as variables (remote_write_targets = ["https://prom-remote.prd", "https://prom-next.prd"]).

Example Terraform snippet (as text):
module "prometheus_server" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//prometheus-server?ref=v1.8.0"
  name   = "prom-primary"
  remote_write_targets = [var.remote_write_primary, var.remote_write_secondary]
  retention_seconds = 604800
}
Notes: pin module by tag and only bump ref after canary testing. Keep the module lightweight: the module should not mutate collector configs.

Grafana provisioning and dashboard lifecycle
- Keep dashboards in a dashboards/ directory in the infra repo as JSON/YAML.
- Use Grafana provisioning (config maps) and a Terraform resource that uploads dashboards on apply.
- Dashboard changes should be small: add a new panel as a separate PR to allow quick reverts.

Provisioning example (text):
resource "kubernetes_config_map" "grafana_dashboards" {
  metadata { name = "grafana-dashboards" namespace = var.grafana_ns }
  data = {
    "service-health.json" = file("./dashboards/service-health.json")
  }
}

Log shipping migration guidance
Options we encounter in private deployments:
- OTEL Collector -> file sink or S3 with lifecycle rules
- Fluent Bit -> aggregator -> S3 or dedicated SIEM
- Vector -> preferred when local indexing is needed due to smaller memory footprint

When migrating log sinks:
1) Introduce dual-output in the collector/agent to ship to old and new destinations.
2) Add identity metadata to new sink events (collector.version, migration-ticket) to filter and validate.
3) Run downstream verification: sample queries and count unique ids over 24–72 hours.
4) Validate access policies and KMS keys in the private environment before final cutover.

Terraform module design notes (practical rules)
- Single responsibility: modules should do one thing (e.g., prometheus-server, otel-collector, grafana-provisioning).
- Inputs are stable primitives: names, image tags, replica counts, exporter endpoints. Avoid passing raw config blobs unless necessary.
- Provide a boolean flag for "dual_write_mode" so rollout automation can toggle mirroring.
- Keep upgrade hooks: a lifecycle_pre_apply script that snapshots Prometheus TSDB and collects Prometheus snapshots (prometheus snapshot command) and uploads to a stable object store in the VPC.
- Use terraform state locking (remote backend in private S3 or vault-enabled DynamoDB style) and document restore steps.

Prometheus snapshot checklist (manual)
1) kubectl exec -n monitoring prometheus-0 -- /bin/promtool tsdb snapshot /prometheus/snapshots || note error
2) tar and gzip snapshot dir, upload to s3://redwood-private-telemetry-backups/<cluster>/<date>.tar.gz
3) Verify snapshot size and list of series_count.

Rollback plan (conservative)
- If canary detects >2% error-rate delta or doubling of retry queues within 24 hours, revert to legacy collector by:
  1) flip traffic routing (DNS/service selector) back to legacy pods,
  2) keep new collector in read-only mode (mirror off) for 72 hours for diagnostics,
  3) revert Terraform by applying the prior state tag and redeploy.

Monitoring runbook (what to watch for first 72 hours)
- Error budgets and SLO indicators (latency for inference-related metrics).
- Increase in exporter latency or retry counts.
- Scrape failures >0.5% of targets for >10 minutes.
- Alert thresholds: otel_exporter_retry_count > 500 (investigate), prometheus_target_scrape_failures > 0.5%

Testing & verification recipes
- Synthetic traffic: run load generator that emits labelled metrics and logs. Verify parity with SQL-like queries in long-term store.
- Backfill test: if switching remote store, confirm that historical queries within the retention window return consistent results.
- End-to-end trace tests: inject a synthetic trace and follow it through collector -> trace backend -> APM UI.

Housekeeping & follow-ups
- Add automated dashboard comparing old_vs_new collector metrics (cpu, mem, exporter_retry_count) to infra repo.
- Schedule a retrospective 2 weeks post-rollout to capture operator notes and module improvements.
- Create a churn ticket to remove legacy exporters after N days of stable operation (default: 14 days).

Open questions for team
- Do we standardize on one log shipper for all private deployments (Vector vs FluentBit)? Pros/cons and operational cost estimates needed.
- Should we add a small Kafka-like buffer inside the VPC to smooth ingestion spikes?

Appendix: useful commands (copy/paste friendly)
- Snapshot Prometheus: kubectl exec -n monitoring prometheus-0 -- promtool tsdb snapshot /prometheus/snapshots
- Check collector exporter queue metrics: kubectl port-forward svc/otel-collector 8888:8888 && curl localhost:8888/metrics | grep exporter_queue_length
- Exporter retry count query (PromQL): sum(rate(otel_collector_exporter_retry_count[5m])) by (exporter)
